app.title: Trustworthy Process Monitor
app.tagline: Data reliability with a human in the loop. Raw data stays on this machine.
status.egressPossible: derived artifacts may leave through the guard
role.pick.basic: Only the essentials: what is wrong, what to do. No lists, no tables. Blue colour scheme.
settings.modeIntro: The mode sets how much the pages show and gives the app its colour: Basic (blue) shows only the essentials, Operator (green) adds charts and tables under 'Show technical analyses', Engineer (violet) shows everything including the decision log.
settings.modelsIntro: Which local model writes the explanations, download another one, or install Ollama.
settings.textSizeHelp: The whole page grows or shrinks; boxes and charts rearrange themselves.
brief.basicNote: Basic mode shows only the essentials.
role.pick.title: Who is looking?

role.pick.name: Your name
role.pick.operator: What is wrong, where, what to do, how sure we are; charts and tables under 'Show technical analyses'. Green colour scheme.
role.pick.engineer: Everything: evidence tables, detector details, relations, the decision log, hash-chain verification, egress ledger and overrides audit. Violet colour scheme.
role.pick.reviewer: Adds the decision log, hash-chain verification, egress ledger and overrides audit.

dq.why.unit_shift: scale change, looks like a different unit
dq.why.relation_break: no longer moves with its related signals
dq.checksHelp: Each row is one check on one batch. Click a row to ask about it; ids in the text are links.
diag.why.process: Several related signals moved together and kept their usual relations: the disturbance is in the process, not in one instrument.
diag.why.sensor: One signal broke its usual relation to its partners while the partners stayed consistent: the instrument, not the process, is the likely cause.
diag.why.data: The change is a data artefact (scale, duplicates, gaps), not a physical event.
diag.why.mixed: Both a process disturbance and an instrument problem remain plausible.
diag.why.unknown: The evidence does not favour a process or a sensor explanation.
diag.verdictHelp.supported: The critique found no objection; the confidence stands.
diag.verdictHelp.weakened: The critique raised objections; the confidence was lowered.
diag.verdictHelp.rejected: The critique found the diagnosis unconvincing; treat it as a hypothesis only.
ass.gainHelp: about {n} points more {metric} on a 0–100 scale

ass.learningCurveHelp: How {metric} grows as more of the data is used; a curve still rising means more data would help.

ass.dqHelp: Share of batches passing each family of checks.
ass.diminishing: diminishing returns from {p} of the data
ass.noThin: No thin regime: every operating state is well represented.
ass.recHelp: Each recommendation names its expected effect and evidence. Nothing is applied before you approve it.

live.intro: Follows a data file or link that keeps getting new lines and checks every sensor once per analysis cycle. It needs no run and is independent of the pages above.
live.empty.title: Nothing is being monitored yet
live.empty.body: Start the built-in demo, or open Settings to replay a file, follow a live link, or watch a growing file.
live.empty.role: An engineer can start a data source.
live.advice.title: Suggested next steps
live.advice.note: Written by the local model from a short summary of the alarms.
live.sensors.title: Sensors, most off-normal first
live.sensors.hint: Every sensor is checked four ways, not only by its average. Level: how far the average is from normal. Trend: is it moving steadily away. Noise: is it more jumpy (or quieter) than normal. Range: how many readings are outside what was seen while learning. The worst check decides the status. Click a row for details.
live.detail.title: Sensor details and history
live.detail.pick: Pick a sensor in the table.
live.detail.chart: One point per analysis cycle. The line stays inside the bands while the sensor is normal. Green band: watch limit. Orange band: alarm limit.
live.events.title: What changed
live.event.settings: {who} set the sensitivity: watch {watch}, alarm {alarm}, noise ×{noise}, range {range}%.
live.set.sens.title: 1. Sensitivity: what counts as “not normal”?
live.set.sens.hint: How far may a sensor move from its learned normal before it is flagged? Type the numbers yourself, or let the AI choose them. Changes apply at once to the latest analysis and stay saved.
live.set.range: Range: flag when (% of readings out of range)
live.set.ai.busy: The local model is choosing the thresholds… this can take up to a minute.
live.set.ai.done: Done. The AI chose these values and they are already applied.
live.set.ai.note: The AI is the local model on this computer. It sees only a short summary of how each sensor behaved while learning (spread, wander, noise), never raw readings. Its choice stays inside safe limits, it explains itself, and you can change the numbers afterwards. It needs the learning cycles to be finished first.
live.set.saved: Saved. It is applied to the latest analysis at once.
live.set.by.default: Default values are in use. Set your own, or let the AI decide.
live.set.by.ai: Currently chosen by the AI ({model}) at {time}. {reason}
live.sim.title: 2. Simulate with a file
live.sim.hint: Test the monitor with a file you already have, even a very large one. It is played back line by line at the speed you choose, as if a plant were writing it live.
live.sim.drop: Drop a CSV file here, or click to choose one
live.sim.dropHelp: Very large files: dropping copies the file into the workspace first, which takes a while. Typing the full path below is faster, then nothing is copied.
live.sim.rows: Rows to play (0 = to the end)
live.sim.calc: About {rows} rows per analysis cycle. Learning takes {n} cycle(s) = {dur}, so the first {first} rows should be normal operation.
live.sim.note: Starting a simulation makes the monitor learn “normal” again from the first cycles, so the first rows should be normal operation.
live.sim.uploadFailed: Upload failed. Is the server still running?
live.sim.started: Simulation started. Open the Monitor tab to watch it.
live.link.title: 3. Live data: paste a link or file path
live.link.hint: For a real dataset that gets a new line about every second. Paste a web link (http or https) to the CSV, or the path of a CSV file that another program keeps writing to. Only the new lines are picked up.
live.link.connected: Connected. New rows are analysed every cycle. Open the Monitor tab to watch.
live.link.note: The link must return CSV text: a header line, then one line per reading, with new lines added at the end (JSON or web pages do not work). If the server allows it, only the new part is downloaded each second, otherwise the whole file is downloaded again (limit 100 MB). Links that need a login are not supported. This is the only place where the app contacts the network, and only to download from the link you give; nothing is sent out.
live.msg.trend.rising.cycle: Trend: rising steadily, {v}{u} within this cycle.
live.msg.trend.rising.three: Trend: rising steadily, {v}{u} over the last 3 cycles.
live.msg.trend.falling.cycle: Trend: falling steadily, {v}{u} within this cycle.
live.msg.trend.falling.three: Trend: falling steadily, {v}{u} over the last 3 cycles.
live.msg.noise.jumpy: Noise: readings are {r}x more jumpy than normal.
live.msg.noise.quiet: Noise: readings vary only {r}x as much as normal (unusually quiet).
live.msg.range.out: Range: {v}% of readings are outside the min-max seen while learning.
live.msg.range.ok: Range: inside what was seen while learning.
live.msg.missing: {v}% of its readings were empty this cycle.
live.msg.dead.changes: Value did not change at all this cycle, but it normally does. Check the sensor.
live.msg.dead.flat: Has been completely flat since monitoring began. Check the sensor.
live.msg.kind.slow: Slow analyzer (updates only every few readings)
live.msg.prof.jumpy: is jumpy / noisy from reading to reading
live.msg.prof.level.stable: normal level very stable (spread is {rel}% of its level)
live.msg.prof.level.fairly: normal level fairly stable (spread is {rel}% of its level)
live.msg.prof.level.varies: normal level varies a lot (spread is {rel}% of its level)
live.msg.prof.unit: unit unknown (not stated in the file)
live.msg.verdict.watch: {n} sensor(s) are slightly off normal. Keep an eye on them.
live.msg.verdict.drift: The process is drifting away from normal. {n} sensor(s) are in alarm, most affected first: {list}.
live.msg.verdict.quality: {n} sensor(s) look broken: {list}. This is a sensor problem, not a process problem, and these sensors are left out of the drift analysis.
live.msg.verdict.quality.alarm: Separately, {n} other sensor(s) are in alarm, so the process may also be drifting: {list}.
live.msg.verdict.untrusted: {n} of {total} sensors look broken (dead or missing data). The data can no longer be trusted, so no process diagnosis is made. Fix the data source first.
live.msg.verdict.gap: Only {rows} rows arrived in this cycle (about {expected} expected). The data stream has gaps or has stopped, so nothing below can be trusted until it recovers.
live.msg.verdict.learn: Learning what normal looks like ({done} of {total} cycles). Alerts start after that.
live.msg.verdict.wait: Waiting for the first analysis cycle to finish.
live.msg.verdict.nosource: No data source yet. Choose one on the Settings tab.
live.msg.verdict.stopped: The data source was stopped. Choose another one on the Settings tab.
live.msg.sig.imminent: Drifting towards a known failure type: {name} (match {score}%) on {sensors}.
live.msg.sig.occurring: A known failure type is occurring: {name} (match {score}%) on {sensors}.
live.msg.sig.how.jumpy: {r}x more big jumps than normal (sticking / stepping)
live.alarm.title: Alarm
live.alarm.trip.imminent: Drift towards a known failure type is imminent: {name}
live.alarm.cause.none: No known failure type matches. This is a generic drift.
live.alarm.cause.generic: No known failure type matches. Generic pattern: {name}.
live.alarm.cause.quality: Not a process failure: the sensor(s) look broken (dead or missing data).
live.alarm.cause.sure.hypothesis: Hypothesis (the catalogue is less sure of it), match {score}%.
live.alarm.cause.partial: {present} of its {n} sensors are in this file.
live.alarm.cause.imminentNote: Not there yet: the pattern is building up ({dir}).
live.alarm.sug.generic.drift: Check the process unit behind the leading sensor first (feed, set-point, utility). If nothing changed in the process, check the sensor itself. Hold set-points and inform the shift engineer.
live.alarm.sug.generic.quality: Check the broken sensor(s): wiring, transmitter, data link. Do not act on the process because of them; they are left out of the drift analysis.
live.alarm.sug.imminent: Act now, before it reaches alarm:
live.alarm.foot: Alarm at {time}. The steps update every analysis cycle; the event list below keeps the history.
live.sig.title: Known failure types: how close is the process to each?
live.sig.hint: Score = how strongly its sensors show the failure's pattern (mean shift, variance increase, collapse, ...). 30% and rising = imminent, 60% = occurring. Failure types whose sensors are not in this file are marked not applicable; some are documented as not visible in the sensors. The catalogue is local data and is never sent to a model.
live.sig.dir: Add your own failure types: drop a YAML file like config/failure_signatures.yaml into {dir} and restart the data source.
live.sig.more: {n} more: not applicable to this file or not visible in sensors
live.demo.teHint: Same demo plant, but the sensors are named like the Tennessee Eastman process and the drift matches Fault 1 (mean shift on xmeas_1, xmeas_4, xmv_3).
live.sim.inject.none: none: play the file as it is
live.sim.inject.auto: auto: mean shift on the first two sensors
live.sim.injectAfter: Inject after (rows; 0 = two cycles after learning)
live.sim.injectHint: The file is played unchanged until then; from that row on the failure's pattern is added to its sensors, so the alarm card can be shown on any file. Failure types whose sensors are not in the file cannot be injected.
live.basic.hint: Basic view: the alarm, the overall state and one chart. Choose another role in the user menu to see every sensor and the settings.
adv.use.partly: Usable, except the rows set aside

und.net.none: No strong connections between sensors were found.
und.unsure.problem: The system is not sure what {name} measures.
und.unsure.reason: Its best guess is “{guess}”, but it is only {pct} sure.
und.unsure.fix1: If you know what it measures, name it; the name is used everywhere from then on.
und.unsure.fix2: Accept or correct the guess so later explanations use the right words.
und.unsure.name: Name this sensor
ass.action.downsample: Use fewer rows (thin out the data)
diag.table.help: Click a row to open the finding above.
diag.table.title: All findings
diag.viz.causeHelp: How many findings have each likely cause. The number in the middle is the total.
diag.viz.groupHelp: The groups with the most findings; click a bar to show only that group in the list.
diag.viz.timelineHelp: Each dot is one finding: further right = later in the data, higher = more serious, colour = likely cause. Click a dot to open it.

dq.faulty.none: No faulty data was found: every check passed.
dq.faulty.title: The faulty data, worst first

dq.score.title: What the % score means
dq.viz.help: Top: how far each batch can be trusted (green = trusted, amber = usable with care, red = not trusted). Bottom: which kind of check found a problem in which batch (grey = nothing found, amber = smaller problem, red = failed). Hover for the reason, click a batch to open it.

und.noHeader: Your file has no header for this column.

brief.topFindingsHelpBasic: Accept, question or override each finding right here.
dq.faulty.moreBasic: {n} further problems are listed in Operator mode.

diag.viz.binnedHelp: Each bar counts the findings in one stretch of the data: further right = later, taller = more findings, colour = likely cause. Click a bar to see those rows.
ass.plain.title: How to make the data better
ass.plain.help: Each strip reads left to right: what limits the analysis, why, and what to do about it. Nothing changes until you approve it.

live.status.finished: finished: no more rows will arrive; the last analysis stays on screen
mon.viz.perSignalHelp: How many events each sensor was involved in; colour = what the sensor probably measures. Click a bar to see what the system knows about that sensor.
